hints.title: Subtree Smallest Tracking
hints.text: Each node requires at least k smaller values strictly within its own subtree.

hints.title: Bounded Subtree Return
hints.text: Return only the k smallest elements from each subtree to keep parent aggregation bounded.

hints.title: Check k-th Element
hints.text: Merge child candidate lists; if the list contains k values and the largest is smaller than node.val, increment the count.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countGreatEnoughNodes(self, root, k: int) -> int:
        ans = 0
        def dfs(node):
            nonlocal ans
            if not node:
                return []
            left_vals = dfs(node.left)
            right_vals = dfs(node.right)
            merged = sorted(left_vals + right_vals)[:k]
            if len(merged) == k and merged[-1] < node.val:
                ans += 1
            return sorted(merged + [node.val])[:k]
        dfs(root)
        return ans
```

variables: n: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Post-order tree traversal returning up to k smallest values from child subtrees.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing the entire subtree for each node separately leads to O(n^2) worst case on skewed trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n * k log k) time by pruning to k smallest elements at each step and O(h * k) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that returning more than k elements from any subtree is unnecessary.
